Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
  SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
  SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
  SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
  SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
  SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
  SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
  SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
  SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
  SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
  SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
  SPA-N-014: Category separation
  SPA-N-015: Title verification
  SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Overarching observation:** The Seller's cover note ("Bluefen consent is addressed", "Riverlark will be released", bonuses "a matter for the Seller", package is "fair and balanced") is contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter, which confirms no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, AUD 420k of bonuses omitted from funds flow, and an unresolved privacy incident. Treat the cover note as advocacy, the Disclosure Letter as the real evidence. The DL's reservation at [11] and [1.4] also confirms the Seller is not standing behind any of these as resolved.

---

| Ref | Issue | Seller position | Buyer should want | Recommendation (reason) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001** | General liability cap | 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) | 30–50% of price (AUD 7.2m–12m); this is a tech business with concentrated revenue (Bluefen ~30%) and open IP/data issues | **Reject; counter at 40% (AUD 9.6m), floor 30%** – 20% is low-end for an AUD 24m private tech deal with multiple unresolved known risks. |
| **SPA-N-002** | De minimis & basket | AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k basket; excess-only recovery | De minimis ≤ AUD 10k (~0.04%); basket ≤ AUD 120k–240k (0.5–1%); **tipping/first-dollar** basket; related claims aggregated | **Counter: AUD 10k / AUD 150k tipping, series-of-claims aggregation** – a 25k de minimis would strip out most realistic single warranty breaches in a business of this size. |
| **SPA-N-003** | General claims time limit | 18 months | 24 months minimum (covers two audit cycles post-Completion); tax 7 years; IP/data 3+ years | **Counter at 24 months general** – 18 months may expire before the first full-year post-Completion audit surfaces issues. |
| **SPA-N-004** | Fundamental/Title regime | Capacity & title subject to same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity" | Title/capacity/authority warranties capped at **100% of price**, time-limited only by statute (6 yrs NSW; consider deed for 12 yrs); outside basket/de minimis | **Reject outright** – if title fails the Buyer has nothing; recovering 20% of price for a 100% title failure is uncommercial and off-market. |
| **SPA-N-005** | Fraud carve-out | None – cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 limitations apply "to all Claims of any nature"; cl 12.3 applies all limits to all Claims unless stated | Express carve-out: no cap, basket, time limit, non-reliance or exclusive-remedy provision applies to fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, dishonesty or wilful concealment by Seller or its officers | **Insist – non-negotiable** – purporting to cap or exclude liability for fraud is contrary to public policy and the drafting as proposed is a red flag in itself. |
| **SPA-N-006** | Disclosure scope | General disclosure of entire data room (DD-002–DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers, and all public registers (DL [1.1]–[1.2]) | Only **specific, fair disclosure** in the DL with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify nature and scope; data room disclosed only via an indexed, agreed USB/schedule and only as fairly disclosed; no general disclosure of public registers; DD-010 ledger etc. not treated as disclosing conclusions | **Reject general data-room/public-register disclosure; accept "fairly disclosed" standard** – blanket disclosure converts every open DD item into a Seller defence and guts the warranty package. |
| **SPA-N-007** | Buyer knowledge qualifier | Cl 8.3: no claim for any matter Buyer or advisers knew of, **including matters discoverable** from data room or public records | Delete; or at most limit to **actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals** of a matter *and* that it constitutes a breach, excluding advisers and constructive/"discoverable" knowledge; expressly preserve claims re matters identified in DD (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006) | **Reject; delete cl 8.3** – "discoverable" knowledge plus general data-room disclosure (N-006) would make the warranties effectively unenforceable. |
| **SPA-N-008** | Bluefen consent | Cover note: "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery of written consent. DL [2]: **no consent, no evidence cl 11.3 conditions satisfied** | Hard **Condition Precedent**: unconditional written Bluefen consent (cl 11.2) with cl 11.3 conditions satisfied/waived, in agreed form, before Completion; Seller to use **best/all reasonable endeavours**; Buyer walk right or price adjustment/escrow if not obtained | **Insist on CP with Buyer waiver right only** – Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / 30% of revenue; a 100% share sale without consent risks losing the anchor customer. |
| **SPA-N-009** | Riverlark facility | ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion"; DL [3]: not repaid, no discharge | Debt-free/cash-free means repayment and **release/discharge of security at or before Completion** as a Completion deliverable; payoff letter in agreed form; amount deducted from price in funds flow; PPSR discharges lodged; change-of-control (cl 8.1) consent or waiver pre-Completion | **Reject post-Completion release** – Buyer would otherwise acquire a company in default under cl 8.1 with AUD 3.2m secured debt and no leverage to compel discharge. |
| **SPA-N-010** | Employee bonuses | AUD 420k closing bonuses "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow; DL [5]: not in funds flow; on-costs unknown | Treat as **Transaction Cost/Debt-like item** in the price: deduct AUD 420k **plus super, payroll tax and PAYG on-costs** (est. ~AUD 480–500k gross) from price or have Seller fund at Completion; specific indemnity for any shortfall; confirm triggering/retention conditions | **Insist on price deduction or Seller-funded payment with indemnity** – the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) is the legal payer; "a matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless reflected in funds flow. |
| **SPA-N-011** | Ironquay IP indemnity | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment (AUD 180k) and "adequate"; DL [4]: no receipt, no confirmatory assignment | **CP/Completion deliverable**: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay; broad **specific indemnity** (outside cap/basket/time limit) for any failure of title to Project Materials, re-development costs, third-party claims, and loss of Bluefen/other contracts dependent on that IP; IP warranties uncapped or at higher cap | **Reject "adequate"** – the exposure is loss of ownership of core deliverables, not the AUD 180k fee; the indemnity must cover consequences, not just the invoice. |
| **SPA-N-012** | Export/privacy incident | "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material"; DL [6]: ~1,240 records sent to unintended external address; access, scope and notification status unknown | Completed investigation report (incl. link-access logs) before signing; Seller to make any OAIC/affected-party notification required under the Privacy Act NDB scheme **pre-Completion**; **specific indemnity** (uncapped, 6-year) for regulatory penalties, notification costs, remediation, customer claims and contract terminations arising from DD-006; data/privacy warranties at higher cap | **Insist on specific indemnity + pre-Completion investigation** – the Seller's own DL refuses to characterise the incident, so the Buyer cannot accept the Seller's "not material" conclusion. |
| **SPA-N-013** | Sandbar renewals | Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary course" | Confirm terms, termination rights and whether DD-008/DD-011 reflect a single arrangement split to sit under thresholds; if committed and not yet accrued/paid, treat as **Debt-like item or price adjustment**; otherwise pre-Completion locked-box/leakage protection and warranty that no non-ordinary commitments were made | **Query and reserve; likely price adjustment for AUD 330k** – the Seller's DL admits it cannot say whether they are unavoidable or ordinary course, so the Buyer should not concede they are. |
| **SPA-N-014** | Category separation | Single regime: all limitations apply to all Claims of any nature (cl 12.3/9.3/12.8/20.5) | Separate regimes: (i) General Warranties – cap/basket/time per N-001–003; (ii) Fundamental/Title/Capacity – 100% cap, statutory limit; (iii) Tax – higher cap, 7 years; (iv) **Specific Indemnities** (Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Sandbar) – outside cap, basket, de minimis, knowledge and disclosure; (v) Fraud – no limits | **Insist** – a one-size-fits-all regime is designed to let known, quantified risks be cut down by the general cap and basket. |
| **SPA-N-015** | Title verification | Title "evidenced by" Company share register (DD-012); DL [10]: Buyer has not completed own verification | Buyer's own ASIC search, review of constitution, share certificates, any shareholder agreements/options/convertibles and PPSR for share charges (esp. Riverlark security over shares); Seller warranties of sole legal & beneficial ownership, free of Encumbrances, no options/rights, fully paid; original certificates and executed transfer at Completion | **Do not rely on DD-012; verify independently before signing** – a company's own register is not conclusive, and Riverlark's security may extend to the shares. |
| **SPA-N-016** | Tax/IP open terms | "Settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, general disclosure) | **Tax**: full tax indemnity for pre-Completion periods, 7-year limit, cap at 100% of price, not subject to disclosure. **IP**: ownership/non-infringement/open-source/moral-rights warranties; Ironquay-specific indemnity (N-011); 3–6 year limit; higher cap | **Reject; these terms are not settled** – both areas carry long-tail exposure invisible at Completion and are precisely the categories the general regime was not designed for. |

---

## Priority order for the mark-up

1. **Deal-structural (must fix before signing):** N-008 Bluefen CP; N-009 Riverlark pre-Completion discharge; N-010 bonus funds-flow deduction; N-015 independent title verification.
2. **Non-negotiable drafting:** N-005 fraud carve-out; N-004 fundamental warranties regime; N-014 category separation; N-007 delete cl 8.3.
3. **Risk allocation:** N-011 Ironquay indemnity; N-012 DD-006 indemnity; N-016 tax/IP regime; N-006 disclosure standard.
4. **Commercial numbers:** N-001 cap; N-002 thresholds; N-003 time limit; N-013 Sandbar adjustment.

**Suggested covering message to Seller:** The Buyer cannot evaluate the package as "fair and balanced" while the Disclosure Letter confirms that the Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay assignment, bonus funding and the DD-006 investigation are all incomplete. The Buyer's mark-up will treat each as a Condition Precedent, Completion deliverable or specific indemnity outside the general limitations, and will not accept cl 8.3 or any limitation purporting to apply to fraud or title.

Let me know if you want this turned into a formal issues list / mark-up rider in SPA clause order.
